summary:
Hundreds of thousands of people protested across France on Saturday, the third weekend of 'Act III' demonstrations over the rising cost of living and conditions in schools, though other reports put the turnout at tens of thousands. Police fired water cannon and tear gas in Paris, Marseille and other cities, and more than 500 people were arrested. In Germany, youth-led rallies drew tens of thousands in the biggest cities, but reports of looting and rioting in Frankfurt and elsewhere in the evening overshadowed the day.

The FBI said North Korean hackers, known as TraderTraitor, were behind the theft of $6.3 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Binance said it had covered 90% of the losses, while another report put the figure at 95%, and it would resume withdrawals on Sunday. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, government data show more than 5,000 people have died in the Ebola outbreak and more than 10,000 have been infected, with cases recorded in other African countries.

Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against returning to war, in a written statement. The warning follows threats of new strikes from Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu, with Trump suggesting action could come after the US midterm elections. In Spain, a deadly high-speed train collision, the second major rail accident this year, has put Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government under scrutiny weeks before a snap general election.

headlines.title: Hundreds of thousands protest across France over living costs and schools
headlines.summary: Protesters marched across France on Saturday in the third weekend of 'Act III' demonstrations. Police fired water cannon and tear gas in Paris, Marseille and other cities, and more than 500 people were arrested.

headlines.title: Youth-led rallies in Germany turn violent in the evening
headlines.summary: Tens of thousands marched in Germany's biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs. Reports of looting and rioting, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the largely peaceful daytime protests, and organisers have called for more protests.

headlines.title: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3 billion Binance hack
headlines.summary: The FBI said North Korean hackers, known as TraderTraitor, were behind the theft of $6.3 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Binance said it had covered 90% of the losses, while another report put the figure at 95%, and it would resume withdrawals on Sunday.

headlines.title: Ebola deaths in DR Congo pass 5,000
headlines.summary: Government data show more than 5,000 people have died and more than 10,000 have contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, its deadliest outbreak. Cases have also been recorded in other African countries.

headlines.title: Iran warns US and Israel against renewed attacks
headlines.summary: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against returning to war, in a written statement. The warning follows threats from US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of new strikes, with Trump suggesting action could follow the US midterm elections.

headlines.title: Spain train crash hits Sánchez weeks before snap election
headlines.summary: A deadly high-speed train collision in Spain is the second major rail accident this year. It has put Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government's competence on trial just weeks before a snap general election.

headlines.title: Thousands rally in Delhi demanding election chief's resignation
headlines.summary: Thousands protested in New Delhi on Sunday, led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters object to a revision of voter rolls, and the rally was held amid tight security.

headlines.title: Judge dismisses Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
headlines.summary: A federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a story about Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein. The judge said the president was 'grasping at straws'.
